text:
carlos (Product): Quick sync on the Capacity modal tweaks. Want to finalize behavior for inline min/max edits, burst scheduling, and SLO presets. Sketches in Figma: https://figma.redwood/capacity-presets — take a look and flag anything risky.
maya (Design): main aesthetic decision: compact vs roomy row for mobile. I lean compact but still need clear touch targets. Also thinking of adding 3 SLO presets: 'Conservative', 'Balanced', 'Aggressive' with one-line descriptions.
lee (Frontend): keyboard + mouse interactions: allow arrow/plus-minus to nudge numeric min/max, ctrl+arrow for 10x steps, double-click on number to type exact value. For slider drag, support shift to slow down for fine tuning.
rachel (Engineering): debounce rules: UI-only changes shouldn't call backend until user commits (Apply) or stops interacting for 500ms for preview. For cost estimations we can run a lightweight API but rate-limit it.
sam (PM): burst scheduling idea: let users define "Burst window" (duration + startable now / scheduled). UX question: inline scheduler vs separate modal? Research hinted people want quick "Add now for 30m" CTA.
maya (Design): proposal: show primary CTA "Add temporary capacity" with quick presets: 15m, 30m, 1h, Custom. If custom selected, open tiny popover with number input + recurrence toggle. Keep copy: "Temporary capacity is billed while active."
lee (Frontend): accessibility: use aria-live region to announce when burst starts/stops and when preview updates. Also ensure slider has role=slider + aria-valuetext like "SLO target: 120 ms" so screenreaders say units.
accessibility-bot: Checklist: 1) sliders must announce new value on keyboard change, 2) tooltips should be accessible via focus, 3) contrast for the SLO preset pills >= 4.5:1, 4) Ensure the "Apply" button is reachable by keyboard before the confirmation modal.
rachel (Engineering): guardrails: we should show a contextual hint when users pick aggressive SLO or huge burst durations. Suggest inline banner: 'Estimated daily instance-hours + cost delta' with a small graph icon. Only block on safety issues (e.g., if requested GPUs exceed pool quota).
carlos (Product): copy for presets — Maya can you draft short lines. I want the labels to avoid jargon: maybe 'Conservative — lower cost, higher latency', 'Balanced — default', 'Aggressive — low latency, higher cost'.
maya (Design): copy draft: Conser vative: "Lower throughput, lower cost." Balanced: "Default for most workloads." Aggressive: "Best latency; higher cost." I'll push these to Figma.
lee (Frontend): microcopy for burst CTA: change "Burst" to "Temporary capacity" and tooltip: "Adds GPUs for short spikes. Billed while active." Also make the scheduling popup announce the end-time.
sam (PM): per-pool presets came up in customer calls. Can we expose a "Save as pool default" checkbox in the Apply flow? If yes, show a small confirmation: "Save as default for pool X" with short link to docs.
rachel (Engineering): backend note: saving defaults per-pool will require small API change + migration. Might be a follow-up. For this PR let's show the checkbox but disable it until API ready, with tooltip: "Coming soon".
accessibility-bot: Additional: ensure focus trap in scheduling popover and that color-only indicators aren't the only signal for status (add icons/labels).
maya (Design): layout nit — move SLO presets above slider so people can pick a preset before fiddling with numbers. For narrow screens collapse presets into a dropdown.
lee (Frontend): agree. Implementation plan: component variations for compact vs regular. Also need tests: keyboard e2e for slider + presets + burst flow.
rachel (Engineering): metrics: capture telem events for: preset used, manual edit, burst scheduled, saved-as-default clicked. We'll need to map to analytics schema.
carlos (Product): final decision checklist: 1) Keep SLO presets, 2) Add quick burst presets (15/30/60), 3) Show cost preview banner when changes are large, 4) Show "Save as pool default" but disabled with tooltip for now. Anyone object?
sam (PM): no objections. small ask: add a soft nudge if preset is 'Aggressive' with copy: "High cost expected" and a link to cost estimator.
maya (Design): will add the nudge pill with hover copy and an icon. Also I'll update spacing and push responsive frames.
lee (Frontend): action items: implement keyboard behaviours, aria-live announcements, and compact component. I'll add storybook stories and axe checks.
rachel (Engineering): action items: debounce + rate-limit preview API, telemetry hooks, and quota checks.
carlos (Product): maya, please update Figma by EOD. Lee & Rachel, let's aim for a dev review early next week. Thanks all. :rocket:
